model.plain: The model lost to the closing line out of sample and the fitted weight on the model is at or below zero, so its disagreement with the market carried no information in the test window. Publishing a model-vs-market difference as an 'edge' is not supported by this evidence.

strategies.plain: 0 of 12 strategies passed every gate. The best paper score is negative (-3.85% lower-bound ROI), which is the ranking's own way of saying no strategy is yet better than luck.
strategies.best: S11 Under in divisional games with total 47+

gates.rule: Every input file pinned by URL and sha256.
Rule fixed before evaluation; no threshold search.
Positive ROI across the two most recent seasons.
Benjamini-Hochberg q < 0.10 against break-even win rate.
At least 60% of tested seasons positive.
Max drawdown no worse than -25 units.

parlay.note: Same-game legs are not independent. Use the phi value to adjust a 2-leg same-game parlay: P = p1p2 + rho*sqrt(p1(1-p1)p2(1-p2)).

strategies.rewards: Points are awarded for statistically defensible performance, not raw ROI: 100 x max(0, lower 95% ROI bound) + 20 x seasons positive + 10 x gates passed. Strategies failing G3 (n<100) score zero. No cash, no prizes: this is a paper competition. Legal review is required before any real reward.

availability.plain: The league publishes injury status for players but publishes no depth chart (the league URL 404s). Only club sites do. So a statement like 'the third-string corner is starting' can be verified for 2 of 26 clubs this week, and is an assumption elsewhere. The model flags 117 players as impacted starters; only 86 of them carry an official game designation, the other 31 are practice-only reports that the league has not yet converted into an availability ruling.

props.plain: 323 prop lines for 323 players, all built from the player's own shrunk usage and the opponent's defensive rating. No prop price exists in any connected source, so no prop edge can be claimed and the market column is deliberately blank.

power.note: This is the arithmetic that decides whether a leaderboard can be ranked on one season. It says a 1% edge cannot be separated from luck in a single season, so any reward scheme must use multi-season samples or lower its ambition.

fillable.question: Which line does the site publish by default: pure model, market, or both?
fillable.already_have: 14 Week 10 own lines with 95% bands; a blend test fitted on 2025 and tested on 2026 giving the market weight 1.336 and the model weight -0.328, with hybrid MAE 9.54 against market-only 9.49.
fillable.what_changes_the_answer: Nothing measurable. The blend test already says the model adds no incremental information over the closing line in the test window.
fillable.options: A: publish the pure model line, labelled as a baseline to beat. B: publish both, model first. C: publish the hybrid.
fillable.recommended: B already happens on the Lines page. The open decision is a one-line policy statement on the Overview: the site must not describe a model-vs-market difference as an edge when the model weight is negative.
fillable.unblocks: The wording of every 'edge' and 'signal' column on the Overview and Lines pages.

fillable.question: What counts as a starter while the league publishes no depth chart?
fillable.already_have: Official injury report: 279 player rows this week. Club depth charts: available for KC and SEA in string order (1st-4th). League site /teams/<club>/depth-chart returns 404 (recorded).
fillable.what_changes_the_answer: Only the site's own transcription budget: 30 more club depth charts would make 'starter' mean 'listed 1st string on the club's own page' for all 32 clubs.
fillable.options: A: define starter = depth rank 1 where a club chart exists, otherwise blank. B: define starter by snap share once snap counts are ingested. C: drop the starter label and publish only official game designations.
fillable.recommended: A, immediately. It removes an assumption the site currently makes (113 'starters' flagged) without needing a new feed, because the two clubs that do have charts prove the definition works.
fillable.unblocks: The 'starters flagged' KPI, the attrition index, and the backup-replacement table.

fillable.question: Does an official game designation or a practice report carry the signal?
fillable.already_have: This week the official page prints a game designation on 6 of 279 rows and a practice status on 279 of 279. The model currently weights practice-only rows (DNP 0.5, limited 0.2) as if they were availability.
fillable.what_changes_the_answer: Nothing for this week's snapshot: the official page is mid-week and has not filed game statuses yet. The answer changes only after Friday/Saturday filings.
fillable.options: A: publish practice-only lines as 'practice only' and exclude them from availability maths. B: keep the weighting but publish it as an assumption. C: wait for game designations before publishing availability at all.
fillable.recommended: A. The page already labels them; the maths should stop treating them as availability.
fillable.unblocks: The attrition index and every 'starters impacted' count.

fillable.question: What may the leaderboard reward, given no odds source is connected?
fillable.already_have: 12 strategies scored against consensus closing lines with 8 gates, bootstrap intervals and Benjamini-Hochberg correction. 0 pass, 2 on watch. No book-level price anywhere in the repository.
fillable.what_changes_the_answer: A licensed odds feed would let ROI be computed against a price that could actually have been taken. Survey data already in the repo (13 official bet-type facts) says most parlay money is lost.
fillable.options: A: paper points only, no cash value. B: cash prizes after legal review. C: no leaderboard until a priced feed exists.
fillable.recommended: A now, with the reward table published as 'paper only'. Any cash structure needs legal review (already flagged F05).
fillable.unblocks: The reward table on the Leaderboard page and whether ranks can be shown at all.

fillable.question: Which of the four existing sites is the one that gets published?
fillable.already_have: Four generations now live in one repository: root pages (two generators), docs/, referee/, verified-lab/. Each was built by a different session and each re-states the same brief differently.
fillable.what_changes_the_answer: Nothing: the duplication is a publishing decision, not a data problem. The new Decision Room index links every generation so nothing is lost.
fillable.options: A: one canonical site, others archived behind a clearly labelled link. B: keep all four and link them (current state). C: merge page by page.

fillable.question: What is the authority order when the league page and a club page disagree?
fillable.already_have: This week: the league injury page lists players, club depth charts list strings, and club sites are on the NFL platform but publish independently. No conflict was observed in the two clubs read, but no rule exists for one.
fillable.what_changes_the_answer: A single observed conflict would settle it by example; none exists yet, which is exactly why the rule has to be chosen in advance.
fillable.options: A: league page wins for status, club page wins for depth order. B: newest timestamp wins. C: publish both and flag the conflict.

contradictions.finding: Four Indianapolis Colts practice cells disagree with the official page, and both repo datasets make the same four errors: A.J. Haulcy (page: Full; repo: DNP), Jonathan Taylor (page: Full; repo: Limited), Jerry Tillery (page: DNP; repo: Limited), Charvarius Ward (page: Full; repo: DNP).
contradictions.impact: Two independent extractions agreeing on a wrong value is the failure mode this project is built to catch. Any availability or prop number built on these four players inherits the error.
contradictions.needs: A second human read of the Colts section of the official page, then a corrected transcription plus a parser test.
contradictions.blocks: The availability table for IND, and any prop line for Taylor, Tillery or Ward.

contradictions.finding: The automated scrape is missing three players the official page lists: BJ Green II (JAX, DE), CJ Allen (IND, LB), Grover Stewart (IND, DT). The page shows 279 player rows; the scrape captured 276.
contradictions.impact: A dropped row is invisible on the site: the player simply never appears, so no blank is rendered and nothing looks wrong.
contradictions.needs: Parser fix plus a completeness assertion (row count per club section) in the scrape stage.
contradictions.blocks: Completeness of the injury feed; the site now checks per-club counts and flags the gap.

contradictions.finding: The hand transcription data/verified/injury_report_2026_week10.tsv is missing 25 official rows: the entire Seattle section (15 rows), the entire Cincinnati section (4), Dre Greenlaw and Christian McCaffrey (SF), Andrew Wingard (AZ), plus the three rows X02 names.
contradictions.impact: This file is used as a verification fixture. A fixture that silently drops whole clubs makes the feed it 'verifies' look better than it is.
contradictions.needs: Re-transcription of the five affected sections, or the fixture replaced by data/evidence/injuries_week10.json.
contradictions.blocks: Any claim that the automated feed was verified against an independent transcription.

contradictions.finding: data/injuries.json holds 61 of the 279 official rows (it covers only the first eight club sections) but is presented next to full-coverage tables.
contradictions.impact: Reading it as a full report understates league-wide injuries by more than three quarters.
contradictions.needs: A coverage label on every page that renders it, or completion.
contradictions.blocks: Nothing, once labelled; it is a partial transcription by design.

contradictions.finding: Two different generators both write index.html. tools/build.py writes a 'NFL1 decision dashboard' page and pipeline/gen_site.py writes an 'Overview · NFL Decision Lab' page. Whichever CI job runs last decides what the site is.
contradictions.impact: Navigation, styling and the numbers on the landing page change depending on job order. A reader cannot know which build they are looking at.
contradictions.needs: One owner per page, enforced by a build check that fails when two generators claim the same file.
contradictions.blocks: Any statement about what the published landing page contains.
contradictions.resolved_this_session: tools/check_generators.py now parses every generator, and the landing page is generated once from a single entry point.

contradictions.finding: The scheduled data job commits new data/model/*.json but never re-renders HTML, so the published pages keep the numbers from the last manual build. Proof: data/model/dashboard.json is stamped 2026-11-12T18:53 while the committed index.html says 'Data built 2026-11-12T05:07:59'. The live New England row reads Out 2 / practice-only 6; the same page regenerated from the committed data reads Out 1 / practice-only 7.
contradictions.impact: Every published number can be up to a day stale with no visible warning. A stale injury number is worse than a missing one because it looks current.
contradictions.needs: Render in the same job that commits the data, and a CI check that fails when a page stamp is older than the data stamp.
contradictions.blocks: Trust in every number on the site.
contradictions.resolved_this_session: The refresh job now renders and commits pages, and an automated stale-page gate fails the build on any mismatch.

contradictions.finding: On the Overview the market column is printed as a bare number (e.g. 2.5, -8.5, -9.5) next to a signed home-team model line, under a note that says 'positive line = home team favoured'. For LA @ ARI the model says ARI +5.2 while the market prints -9.5, which reads as a 14.7-point edge; the real difference is 4.27 points. The same framing appears on SEA @ LV and MIA @ IND.
contradictions.impact: A reader can be shown a fabricated edge three times its real size. This is the single most decision-relevant defect found in this audit.
contradictions.needs: Print both numbers in the same convention, or print the market as an away-team number with an explicit label, plus a regression test.
contradictions.blocks: Every 'signal' badge on the landing page.
contradictions.resolved_this_session: The dashboard publishes market and model numbers in one stated convention, with a signed away-team column and a test that the printed edge equals the difference of the two printed numbers.

contradictions.finding: The league site publishes no depth chart: /teams/<club>/depth-chart returns the 404 'Flag on the Play' page for both clubs tested. Club sites do publish depth charts in string order, so the '1st/2nd/3rd/4th string' requirement is satisfiable, but only club by club.
contradictions.impact: Any league-wide starter/backup table currently rests on two transcribed clubs plus a weekly mirror. The site must say so rather than implying full coverage.
contradictions.needs: 30 more club depth-chart transcriptions (or the weekly mirror, clearly labelled as a mirror).

contradictions.finding: The repo's depth-chart rows put KC running back Kenneth Walker at 1st string and Emmett Johnson at 2nd; the club's official page lists Emmett Johnson 1st and Walker 3rd. Cyrus Allen is 3rd in the repo and 2nd on the club page.
contradictions.impact: A starter/backup label is the input to every 'next man up' claim, so a stale chart mislabels who is actually replacing whom.
contradictions.needs: Confirm which snapshot the mirror row came from, then either re-transcribe from the club page or label the mirror date.

contradictions.finding: The same club appears under different codes across the repository: the league page prints AZ and LA, the model prints ARI and LA, the tsv prints AZ but is missing LAR entirely, and the README of one session notes LAR where another says LA.
contradictions.impact: Any join on club code silently drops rows. This audit's own first run hit it (ARI vs AZ produced a 32-row mismatch before the alias table was added).
contradictions.needs: One canonical code set, with an explicit alias table stored in the repository and tested.
contradictions.resolved_this_session: A single alias map is applied in the verification tool and reported, so a join can no longer drop a club silently.

suggestions.decision_impact: KC WR2/KR/PR rows disagree with the club's own chart (flag LR-02); 2nd/3rd-string replacement reads are wrong until charts are refreshed. A weekly diff against club pages would catch this automatically.

suggestions.title: Add a news-to-status layer: link official news as evidence and flag divergences from the game-status column
suggestions.decision_impact: Darnold is ruled out by official news while the official report row shows practice-only (flag LR-05). Without this layer, availability and next-man-up signals under-state absences in exactly the window decisions are made.

suggestions.title: Show data-freshness stamps on every table that can go stale mid-week (standings, injuries) and state the snapshot cut-off
suggestions.decision_impact: The NYG/WAS rows looked like errors until the retrieval stamps were read (flag LR-01). A visible 'as of <retrieval>' stamp on each table prevents snapshot age being mistaken for bad data and tells a reviewer exactly when to re-verify.

suggestions.title: Cross-check every feed-provided kickoff time against the official schedule before publication
suggestions.decision_impact: LR-07 showed the upstream schedules feed can carry wrong kickoff times while citing the official schedule as source (JAX @ NYG and PIT @ PHI were swapped on 2026-11-13). A kickoff printed on a betting-decision page must come from the official page, so each model refresh should compare every fixture's date and kickoff against the current official capture and block on mismatch.

paths.name: Path A — Data first
paths.summary: Close the open data questions (odds source, depth charts for all clubs, game-level panel, inactives deadline), then build signals.
paths.pros: Every downstream decision rests on verified, point-in-time official data; validation gates become meaningful.
paths.cons: Slower to produce a visible leaderboard; requires repeated official snapshots.

paths.name: Path B — Strategy first
paths.summary: Prototype the 10 candidate strategies and the leaderboard immediately, with all performance values blank until gates pass.
paths.pros: Fastest visible competition framework and reviewer feedback loop.
paths.cons: Risk of optimising on incomplete data; every strategy stays NOT PASSED until the missing official data arrives.

paths.name: Path C — Review only / hold
paths.summary: Implement nothing beyond documentation and the review gate until a reviewer explicitly chooses a path.
paths.pros: Zero implementation risk; maximum review control.
paths.cons: No progress on own lines, signals or leaderboard operation.

gates.name: Provenance
gates.criterion: Every input value has an official source link and retrieval timestamp

gates.name: Point-in-time
gates.criterion: Only data published before the decision timestamp is used; official filing times are respected

gates.name: Pre-registration
gates.criterion: Strategy formula, thresholds and evaluation window are frozen before scoring

gates.name: Minimum sample
gates.criterion: NIST generic advice: 20 observations for a correlation, 32 per group for an average difference, 50 for a standard deviation

gates.name: Out-of-sample
gates.criterion: Model is fit on one partition and assessed on data not used to build it

gates.name: Significance
gates.criterion: Two-sample t-test for equal means with pre-registered alpha and critical region

gates.name: Multiple comparisons
gates.criterion: Every tested strategy is logged so the number of tests is known before scoring

gates.name: Correlation is not causality
gates.criterion: No strategy is described as causal without designed-experiment evidence

gates.name: Parlay/prop correlation guard
gates.criterion: Leg correlations must be measured before combining legs

gates.name: Stability
gates.criterion: Signal must persist across consecutive seasons/weeks

gates.name: Skill over luck
gates.criterion: Performance must exceed a pre-registered skill threshold after all other gates pass

gates.name: Reproducibility
gates.criterion: A script and data snapshot reproduce every published number

gates.name: Deploy integrity
gates.criterion: Every table row has an official source link; no broken internal links; Pages build succeeds
